1) a Bayesian framework for PARAFAC tensor decomposition is proposed; 2) it can be used for tensor completion; 3) the proposed method is able to recover a ground-truth tensor rank; 4) the proposed method can complete brain imaging and gene expression datasets with missing entries.

we proposed a Bayesian framework for tensor completion and extrapolation that can accommodate general models for data distribution, that we derived two algorithms for Gaussian- and poisson-distributed data that minimize the rank regularized least squares and Kullback-Liebler divergence, and that we showed that our technique is able to complete real world brain imaging and yeast expression datasets with 15% and 50% of missing entries, respectively, with recovery errors of -11dB and -15dB.
